name: Base coat nail strengthener

card.summary: A strengthening base coat is a clear or tinted polish layer applied under colour or alone to protect nails, help polish adhere and keep hands looking groomed.
card.aka: nail hardener base; strengthening base coat
card.note: Some nail products have historically contained formaldehyde; check ingredient lists if sensitive.

quick.overview:
A base coat is a clear, milky or pink layer painted onto the nail before colour. Strengthening versions are marketed as hardening and protecting the nail plate so it chips, peels and splits less.

For appearance, healthier-looking nails are part of neat grooming, and a base coat also keeps polish from staining the nail and helps a manicure last.
quick.how: It is brushed on in a thin layer on clean nails, either alone for a natural finish or under colour and top coat. Products are reapplied as the wear shows, and people often use them on short, natural nails.
quick.risks: Reported concerns are skin or nail irritation and allergic reactions to certain ingredients. Formaldehyde has been eliminated from some nail polish brands while others still use it, according to Wikipedia.

lead: A base coat is a clear, milky or opaque pink layer applied before coloured polish. Wikipedia says it helps strengthen nails, restore moisture and help polish adhere, while also preventing staining and extending the manicure's life [1].

Strengthening base coats are sold as nail hardeners that coat the plate to reduce chipping, scratching and peeling, the same protective purpose Wikipedia ascribes to nail polish generally [1]. For people working on grooming, neat natural-looking nails are a low-effort part of the hands' appearance.
Typical polish chemistry is a film-forming polymer, usually nitrocellulose, dissolved in a volatile solvent, with plasticizers, resins and other additives [1].

chain: Clear protective film over the nail plate
Less chipping and peeling, no staining
angle.text: A strengthening base coat adds a protective layer so nails look intact and groomed, with or without colour on top.

paras: Base coats come clear, milky or pink. Some are sold as ridge fillers to smooth uneven nails without buffing, and peel-off versions can be removed without remover [1].

Standard polishes use nitrocellulose in volatile solvents such as butyl or ethyl acetate with plasticizers, pigments and resins [1]. Wikipedia describes formaldehyde as part of the 'toxic trio' with toluene and dibutyl phthalate and notes it has been removed from some brands while others still use it [1].
